Series::detach_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::detach_() const -> Series&

What It Does¶

detach_() detaches the current Series handle in place.

This is the mutating sibling of detach(). Instead of returning a separate detached value and leaving the original handle untouched, it changes the receiver so that future work from this handle no longer follows the earlier reverse-mode path.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series& The current Series, after detaching its reverse-mode state in place.

Reverse-Mode Meaning¶

After detach_() on the current handle:

  • the receiver is no longer tracked

  • later reverse-mode built from that receiver no longer propagates through the earlier path

The important mental model is “this handle becomes a new autodiff boundary.”

That means the numeric value remains, but the reverse-mode history attached to this handle is cut.

Examples¶

Example 1. detach_() clears tracking on the receiver itself.

auto x = pluss::make_series({6.0, 7.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

std::cout << "before=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.detach_();
std::cout << "after=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

before=true
after=false

Example 2. Detaching an intermediate in place blocks the already-built upstream path from receiving sensitivity.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
auto y = x.mul(2.0);
y.detach_();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "x_has_dL_dx=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Before the detach, the chain would have been

y = 2x
L = sum(y)

which ordinarily gives dL/dx = [2, 2, 2].

After y.detach_(), the handle y becomes a new boundary, so the later reverse pass no longer propagates through the earlier x -> y path.

Output¶

x_has_dL_dx=false

Example 3. After in-place detaching, the same handle can be turned into a new tracked leaf.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());
auto y = x.mul(2.0);
y.detach_();
y.tracks_slope_(true);
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "x_has_dL_dx=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "y_dL_dy=" << y.sensitivity() << "\n";

Now the scalar objective is differentiated with respect to the post-detach handle y itself:

L = y1 + y2 + y3

so the new leaf stores [1, 1, 1], while the original upstream source x still receives nothing from this new reverse path.

Output¶

x_has_dL_dx=false
y_dL_dy=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • detach_() mutates the receiver. If you need the original tracked handle to remain unchanged, use detach() instead.

  • This method is about reverse-mode state, not numeric value transformation.

  • After detaching in place, later reverse-mode from that handle no longer populates upstream sensitivity through the earlier graph.

Summary¶

Use detach_() when the current handle itself should stop participating in the existing reverse-mode path and become a fresh boundary for whatever comes next.

See Also¶

  • Series::detach: non-mutating detach that returns a detached value.

  • Series::tracks_slope_: re-enable tracking later if this handle should become a new tracked leaf.
